author: TEDx Talks
description:
Are we stuck in the screen, or does our smartphone usage tell a more complicated story? Drawing on ten years of research, including her 2026 study, Caitlin Begg examines how always-on expectations reshape work, relationships, and social life.... and how the dérive may help.  

Caitlin Begg is the founder of Authentic Social and a sociologist. Authentic Social is a NYC-based applied research lab at the intersection of sociology and technology. Since her undergraduate Harvard sociology thesis in 2016, she has spent the last decade researching how digital communication reshapes human interaction. Caitlin speaks around the U.S. and Europe, presenting her work at venues ranging from the American Sociological Association Annual Meeting to World Summit AI in Amsterdam. She is also the host of the Progression to Analog podcast. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to nurture your phone-free hobbies | Caitlin Begg | TEDxPrincetonU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Survivorship isn't a race. And it shouldn't be measured in marathons," says former eye care provider and professor Dr. Yvette Colón, OD. After pancreatic cancer took both her career and her mobility, she found herself in a wheelchair, facing a world that only wanted to hear one specific story: the medal, the marathon, the triumphant finish line.

In this raw, deeply necessary talk, Dr. Colón dismantles the toxic "warrior" narrative to reveal the hidden emotional tax of performing resilience. She offers an unflinching look at what it's like to fall outside the story you're expected to tell, providing a new framework for learning how to truly live in a completely altered life—on your own terms. We live in a culture that demands heroism from the suffering. From the moment of diagnosis, patients are handed a "warrior" script—a mandate to stay positive, fight hard, and serve as an inspiration to everyone around them. But what happens when the pressure to be "strong" becomes as exhausting
title: The Myth of the Cancer Warrior | Yvette Colón | TEDxKU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We tend to imagine diplomacy happening through speeches, negotiations and conversations behind closed doors. But long before anyone speaks, the buildings where nations meet are already communicating.

Drawing on years of reporting from embassies, diplomatic residences and international institutions around the world, investigative journalist Molly McCluskey explores architectural diplomacy: the long-standing role buildings play in how nations represent themselves and engage with the world. Through examples from across the globe, she reveals how choices about sustainability, materials, landscape and public access allow the built environment to express a nation’s identity, priorities and intentions — and make its response to climate change visible.

At a time when global progress on climate action is faltering, Molly makes the case that buildings can do more than reflect our values. They can model responsibility, influence relationships and help shape a more sustainable, interconnected w
title: When buildings speak | Molly McCluskey | TEDxBrisbane

author: TEDx Talks
description: Children with incarcerated parents are often expected to overcome extraordinary challenges through resilience alone, yet resilience is rarely enough without meaningful support. Drawing from her lived experience, educational research, and work as a school founder, Dr. Christina "Pip" Pipkin explores how schools and communities can become villages of compassion that help break generational cycles of incarceration and create lasting opportunities for children and families. Dr. Christina "Pip" Pipkin is an educator, researcher, and founder of FAYE Learning Center. Drawing from her lived experience as the daughter of an incarcerated parent and nearly 20 years in education, her work explores how schools and communities can become powerful systems of belonging that help children and families break generational cycles. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: More than resilience: Why every child needs a village | Dr. Christina Pipkin | TEDxBessies Creek

description: Grief is not only about death. It shows up after losing a relationship, a career, a dream, a sense of identity, or even a version of yourself you thought you would always be, and most of us were never given language for how we carry it. Loss does not always look like crying, sometimes it looks like never stopping, needing to talk through everything, holding everyone else together, or disappearing into questions with no answers, and when grief goes ignored it becomes Post-Crisis Lag, silently unraveling the person you have been working so hard to keep intact. Leadership strategist Brigitte Brown Jackson introduces the Grief Has a Personality framework, four distinct grief response styles that finally give language to what you may have been living, because if someone has ever made you feel wrong for the way you grieve a loss, this talk was written for you. description: Why do our relationships, cultures, organizations, and institutions keep repeating the same human problems, even when we try sincerely to fix them? Drawing on more than 30 years of experience and research in individual and organizational learning, Jay Clancy reveals a surprising pattern: we’ve spent generations trying to control our humanity instead of learning how to navigate it. “Getting Better at Being Human” invites us to embrace our humanity, learn to stand together in life’s most complex human spaces, and build organizations that help people, communities, and whole societies rise together. For more than thirty years, Jay Clancy has synthesized entrepreneurial leadership, street-tested consulting experience, and multidisciplinary research across diverse disciplines, industries, cultures, and human experiences to better comprehend how people, organizations, and societies learn and grow. title: Getting better at being human | Jay Clancy | TEDxBessies Creek

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world defined by "unpredictability within repeating patterns" (chaos), Dr. Robin Carter challenges us to find a "survival phenotype"—a strategy for flourishing despite inevitable catastrophes. Drawing inspiration from author Paul Kingsnorth, the speech proposes that the key to a worthwhile survival lies in nurturing four traditional human values: Past, Place, People, and Prayer (ultimate value). Using two contrasting examples—our rat-like mammalian ancestor surviving the dinosaur extinction and the character Jamal from Slumdog Millionaire—Carter demonstrates how these 4 Ps equip us for the future. Our cultural heritage (Past) gives us the belief that "dragons can be killed." Knowing and caring for our environment (Place) provides the raw materials for solutions. Community (People) is essential, as "happiness is only real when shared." Finally, our ultimate, unshakable value (Prayer) provides the necessary focus.

title: Surviving with our Humanity Intact | Robin Carter | TEDxJIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are told that AI is our future. We praise every new feature learned by AI chatbots making our lives significantly easier, but its environmental cost is rarely talked about and may even be unknown. This talk reveals the hidden ecological impacts and footprint we leave behind with every AI search we carelessly make.  
 Anna is currently a student who loves spending time outdoors and exploring nature. As a student, using AI has become very common and until recently, she wasn't aware of the ecological impacts of using AI like many of us. Upon finding out, she was determined to find a way to share with friends and others about the impacts that we cause carelessly simply from not knowing. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What AI Is Really Costing Us | Anna Matsuhisa | TEDxJIS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Anxiety is more than just a feeling, it's your brain's phenomenal ability to mentally prepare you for something before it even happens. This talk reframes anxiety through exploring the neuroscience and psychology behind it, and behind chronesthesia, the brain's incredible ability to mentally time travel, ultimately revealing the truth behind anxiety: that it’s not as bad as we think.
 Eden, like most juniors in high school, is extremely familiar with the universal feeling of anxiety. As one of the most common mental health disorders worldwide, she hopes to provide new insight and understanding into why anxiety may not be the villain it is often perceived as, but rather, how it can become something much greater through the use of her own experiences and research. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Mental Time Travel: Rewriting Anxiety | Eden Luu | TEDxJIS Youth

description: Luzy will delve into how social media algorithms subtly shape our perception of truth at TEDxYouth@JIS. Through her talk, she highlights the importance of media literacy. She explores how digital platforms amplify confirmation bias and the mere exposure effect to influence what we perceive as true. Drawing on real-world examples, Luzy demonstrates how misinformation spreads faster than ever before and why it is increasingly difficult to identify. She introduces a simple framework for media literacy — the SIFT method — encouraging the audience to Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, and Trace claims back to their original context. This talk challenges us to ask: Is the algorithm writing our future, or is it time to take the pen back? Luzy Kohnlein is a senior at Jakarta Intercultural School. She has a strong interest in history, law, and the ways information shapes collective belief and individual decision-making. She is passionate about critical thinking and media liter
title: Taking Back the Pen | Luzy Kohnlein | TEDxJIS Youth
